definition: Death taboo is a cultural belief and emotional avoidance around discussing death, which can create fear, moral pressure, and reluctance to talk about end-of-life choices. In this context, it acts as a barrier to open communication and autonomous decision-making about future care.

reasons: The definition states that death taboo “acts as a barrier to open communication and autonomous decision-making about future care.” While the packet supports communication avoidance linked to filial piety and moral pressure/fear triggered by death taboo, it does not clearly support that death taboo specifically creates a barrier to autonomous decision-making (the packet attributes restriction of autonomy primarily to “family-centered decision-making.”).
“Cultural belief” is not supported by the packet; the source describes death taboo as a cultural taboo/pressure, not a belief.

The definition adds a broader claim that death taboo itself is a barrier to autonomous decision-making about future care; the packet only supports a narrower link to fear, communication avoidance, and lower ACP acceptance in end-stage heart failure patients.
